title.narrative: Supporting Safe Returns: Multi-Sectoral Integrated Intervention for Safe and Dignified Return and Community Resilience in Lattakia, Deir-ez-Zor, and Dar’a, Syria.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn line with the strategic priorities under Envelope 2 of the 2025 First standard allocation strategy set by OCHA, PUI proposes a multi-sectoral integrated intervention focused on Shelter, WASH, ERL and FSA sector in selected underserved areas of returns of Lattakia, Deir-ez-Zor and Dar’a Governorates. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe overall objective of the proposed intervention is to support safe and dignified return of displaced population to areas of origin by enhancing access to essential services sustainable livelihoods for returnees and host communities through integrated multisectoral and community led interventions. Protection, AAP, GBV, PSEA prevention, and climate adaptation will be key cross-cutting approaches throughout the whole action. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltugtltbgtShelterlt/bgtlt/ugt: PUI proposes to enhance access to safe, dignified and sustainable shelter solutions for returnees and vulnerable host communities, by conducting repair/rehabilitation of moderately damaged apartments in the targeted areas. In total, PUI will rehabilitate 218 moderate damaged apartments, targeting 1,398 individuals. More specifically, 630 individuals will benefit from enhanced shelter solutions in Jbeileh, Deir-ez-Zor, 288 individuals in Western Mahila, Hrak, Izr’a, Dar’a, and 240 in Rural Qastal Maaf, Qastal Maaf, Lattakia, and 240 in Snobar, Hannadi, Lattakia. Dar’a component was included following thorough community consultations. More specifically, during the implementation of SHF funded project 33247 in Western Mahila, the number of requests for PDAs (Partially Damaged Apartments) rehabilitation exceeded the target. Following direct observation of newly arrived returnees’ families, and discussion with community leaders and returnees, PUI decided to add the shelter component in Western Mahila, Dar’a in order to respond to a direct need highlighted by the targeted community. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltugtltbgtWASH:lt/bgtlt/ugt PUI will increase equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for returnees and local communities Deir-ez-Zor, and Lattakia. More specifically, PUI will rehabilitate water stations with maintenance works for ground reservoirs in two communities of Qastal Maaf, Lattakia, and will conduct the rehabilitation of the sewage network in Masaken Al-Hibz – Jbeileh, Deir-ez-Zor. PUI intervention will directly contribute to increasing dignified living conditions while reducing public health risks for the affected population. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltugtltbgtFSA:lt/bgtlt/ugt In order to strengthen livelihoods and community resilience in crisis-affected targeted areas, PUI will support agri-food income generating activities for 80 people in targeted agricultural areas of rural Lattakia. The support will include capacity building trainings, vocational trainings and conditional cash assistance.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtERL:lt/bgt To enhance economic recovery and support sustainable return, PUI will support 40 entrepreneurs / small business in Deir-ez-Zor. Jbeileh represent an important commercial hub for DEZ city and according to needs and gaps highlighted by local communities (Annex 04) the area is in need to support (technical and financial) to support local businesses. Further, to promote social cohesion and enhance community participation PUI will promote community led initiatives in both Lattakia and Deir-ez-Zor. These initiatives will help bring communities together, reducing tensions and enhancing cooperation. This component is highly needed in sensitive areas which experienced tension following the regime change. Thanks to CLIs, communities will have the opportunity yo lead their own development by proposing ideas and implementing social initiatives.lt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtPUI’s integrated strategy was designed in close coordination with affected communities to provide multisectoral assistance aimed at improving the overall living conditions for returnees and host communities. The proposed project is designed to complement other PUI’s interventions funded by SHF (in Dar’a), UNDP (in Lattakia and Deir-ez-Zor) and by SDC (in Deir-ez-Zor), maximizing the impact of PUI’s integrated area-based approach. ltbrgtlt/pgt
